answers.displayAnswer: No. In ideal linear series resonance, $I_{\mathrm{m}}=U_{\mathrm{m}}/R$. The DC circuit has $U_{\mathrm{DC}}=U_{\mathrm{m}}$, so $I_{\mathrm{DC}}=U_{\mathrm{m}}/R$ and the currents are equal. Do not substitute RMS current for amplitude or compare a startup transient with steady state.

answers.displayAnswer: Inductive coupling between the oscillating-circuit coil and the grid-circuit coil returns the circuit signal to the grid. The grid controls anode current, and the anode circuit replenishes circuit energy. Connection polarity and phase must support oscillation, and feedback strength must overcome losses.

answers.displayAnswer: The energy source is the DC supply; the regulating "valve" is the triode vacuum tube; the oscillating part is the inductance-capacitance circuit; feedback comes from inductive coupling between the circuit coil and grid coil. In stable oscillation, supplied energy replaces the loss each cycle.
